scenes.text: Everybody trains biceps. Then they wonder why their arms still look like cooked spaghetti.
Here's the secret. Your triceps make up two thirds of your upper arm. Train them, and your sleeves start begging for mercy.
Three moves. No fancy equipment. Let's go.
Hands on a bench behind you, fingers forward, legs out. Lower until your elbows hit ninety degrees, then push back up.
Keep your back close to the bench, and don't let your shoulders creep up to your ears. You're a lifter, not a turtle.
Make a diamond with your thumbs and index fingers, right under your chest. Lower slow, press up hard.
Too hard? Drop to your knees. Nobody's watching. Well, I am.
Three sets of eight to ten.
Grab a dumbbell, or a backpack full of books, and hold it behind your head. Elbows point at the ceiling. Extend up, then lower slow.
Feel that stretch? That's where the growth happens.
That's it. Three moves, three sets, twice a week. Give it a month, and watch those sleeves suffer.
Subscribe, and I'll see you on the next rep.
